question: Why was shipment SH-1975 released in June, and did it turn out well?
context:
[memo_dec-140.md]
# Decision memo DEC-140 (2026-09-30)

Subject: CR-3. Disposition: CARRIER PROBATION.

Third Frostline excursion in 30 days (EXC-2040, EXC-2044, EXC-2048). Until 2026-12-31 every Frostline shipment with an excursion is ESCALATED to the QA lead, even if v3 would release it.

[memo_dec-118.md]
# Decision memo DEC-118 (2026-05-02)

Subject: SH-1990. Disposition: RELEASE.

Dip to -0.8 C lasted only 5 min; judged acceptable because it was short. Exception granted without QA lead.

[memo_dec-135.md]
# Decision memo DEC-135 (2026-07-03)

Subject: L-A-04. Disposition: RELEASE.

Cold room 2 door alarm, 40 min at 9.0 C. Stock kept in date. QA lead accepted the deviation and deducted 40 min.

[sop-temp-v2.md]
# Temperature excursion SOP, version 2

Any reading above 8.0 C or below 2.0 C: QUARANTINE the shipment; QA destroys it. No release is allowed.

Owner: Quality Assurance.

answer.reason: Shipment SH-1975 was released in June because the temperature dip to -0.8 C lasted only 5 minutes, which was deemed acceptable by the QA lead. The decision turned out well as no further issues were reported and the stock was kept in date.
answer.trigger: Dip to -0.8 C lasted only 5 min
answer.outcome: Shipment was released and no further issues were reported.
